topics.definition: Data partitioning divides a large dataset into smaller, manageable partitions.
tips: Choose partitions based on access patterns.

topics.definition: Horizontal sharding distributes rows of data across multiple database servers.
topics.example: Users A–M on Shard 1, N–Z on Shard 2
tips: Use when a single database cannot handle growth.

topics.definition: Vertical partitioning separates columns or features into different databases or tables.
topics.example: User profile and login data stored separately
tips: Separate frequently accessed data from infrequently used data.

topics.definition: A shard key determines how data is distributed across shards.
tips: Choose keys that distribute data evenly.

topics.definition: Rebalancing redistributes data when shards become unevenly loaded.
topics.example: Add a new shard and migrate records

topics.definition: Consistent hashing minimizes data movement when nodes are added or removed.
Data migration moves data safely between partitions or shards.
Design partitions carefully, monitor balance and minimize cross-shard operations.
